title: Skeletal Hierarchy Viewer (Procedural Skeleton)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a procedural human skeleton (20 bones), with cylinders representing bone segments and spheres representing joints, supporting hierarchical transformations and interactive selection.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules within <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Skeletal Hierarchy (Must Be Implemented; Names May Match or Use Synonyms)]
Example root structure: root → pelvis → spine → chest → neck → head; chest → L_shoulder → L_upperArm → L_forearm → L_hand; chest → R_shoulder → …; pelvis → L_thigh → L_shin → L_foot; pelvis → R_thigh → …. There must be 20 bones (bone segments) in total, with each segment represented by a CylinderGeometry connecting parent and child joints represented by SphereGeometry.

[Interaction]
(1) Use a Raycaster to select and highlight a bone (or joint) by clicking. Display the following in the DOM element with id="boneInfo": name, parent bone, and bone-segment length (either world-space or local-space length is acceptable, but it must be labeled).
(2) Pose preset dropdown with id="poseSelect": include at least T-pose, rest, and walk (a single frame from a walking cycle; a fixed frame is acceptable).
(3) After selecting a bone, use sliders to adjust its local rotation (Euler angles, consistently using either degrees or radians): id="boneRotX", id="boneRotY", and id="boneRotZ". The recommended range is -π~π or -180~180.

[Rendering]
(4) Include OrbitControls, a ground grid, and a reasonable initial camera position.
(5) Use distinct colors for selected and unselected elements.

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - boneCount: number (should be 20)
  - selectedBone: string | null (name of the currently selected bone, or null if none is selected)
  - currentPose: string (e.g. 'tpose'|'rest'|'walk')
  - bones: Array<{ name: string, parent: string | null, length: number, rotation: { x: number, y: number, z: number } }>

Output a single HTML file.
difficulty_analysis: L5: Hierarchical matrix updates for 20 bones, click picking, pose presets and slider-driven local rotation, and synchronization of __3D_STATE__ with boneInfo.
